note.note:
Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  
  - Low mood, low energy “for a long time.”  
  - Decreased appetite ~3–3.5 months.  
  - Unintentional weight loss ≈1 stone over ≥6 months (approximate).  
  - Intermittent nausea without vomiting; headaches at work.  
  - Episodic palpitations and feeling unable to breathe in elevators; no exertional dyspnea when walking; no chest pain.  
  - Normal bowel habits; no diarrhea, blood, or mucus; no reflux.  
  - Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid) in past; stopped levothyroxine months ago.  
  - Decreased physical activity (“haven’t been walking lately”).  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Not recorded  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  
  - Levothyroxine (thyroxine) — stopped; dose/route/frequency not documented.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  
  - Married; spouse reports concerns with “nightly activities” (suggestive of sexual dysfunction); details not specified.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  
  - Physical activity: markedly reduced recently.  
  - Diet: reduced intake due to poor appetite.  
  - Tobacco/alcohol/substance use: Not recorded  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Not recorded  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  
  - Reports persistent low mood and low energy; uncertain about labeling as “depressed.”  
  - Anxiety-like episodes in elevators with palpitations/air hunger.  
  - No documentation of sleep disturbance, anhedonia screening, or suicidal ideation/self-harm assessment.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  
  - Employed lawyer; changed law firm ~3.5 months ago.  
  - Home life “OK.”  
  - No housing or financial concerns recorded.

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (telehealth)  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:  Not recorded  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:  Not recorded  
- Ear exam including otoscopy:  Not recorded  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated:  Not recorded  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood:  Not recorded

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  
  - Planned: “general set of bloods” including anemia screen (CBC), renal function, liver function, and vitamin levels (exact vitamins not specified).  
  - Fasting glucose/lipids and HbA1c: Not recorded.  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  
  - Planned per clinician.  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Not recorded  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not recorded  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not recorded  
- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not recorded  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not recorded

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary of key findings:  
  - Months-long low mood, reduced energy and appetite, ~1 stone unintentional weight loss, intermittent nausea, headaches.  
  - Situational palpitations/air hunger in elevators; no exertional dyspnea; no chest pain.  
  - History of hypothyroidism; stopped levothyroxine months ago; no recent blood tests.  
  - Bowel habits normal; no red flag GI symptoms reported.  
- Working diagnosis:  
  - Undifferentiated fatigue with anorexia and weight loss; evaluate for relapse of hypothyroidism vs depressive disorder; consider situational anxiety/panic related to elevators.  
- Relevant differentials (consistent with DDx and transcript):  
  - Major depressive disorder or mixed anxiety/depression: Low mood, low energy, decreased appetite, sexual difficulties, functional symptoms (nausea, headaches), weight loss.  
  - Hypothyroidism relapse due to stopping levothyroxine: Fatigue, low mood, decreased libido; weight loss less typical but possible with reduced intake.  
  - Situational panic/claustrophobia: Palpitations and dyspnea specifically in elevators with preserved exertional capacity.  
  - Nutritional deficiency/iron deficiency anemia: Possible contributor to fatigue and headaches given poor intake and weight loss.  
- Considerations (lower likelihood but noted in DDx):  
  - Chronic infection or occult malignancy given weight loss/anorexia; no focal symptoms recorded.  
- Plan from visit:  
  - Order general blood tests (CBC for anemia, renal and liver function, vitamin levels).  
  - Results to be communicated via text; patient to book follow-up upon notification.  
  - Safety advice: Seek urgent care for chest pain or significant palpitations; contact clinic if bowel habit changes or vomiting develops.  
- Conflict noted:  
  - Weight loss and palpitations are less typical of hypothyroidism; clinician noted palpitations more consistent with hyperthyroidism/anxiety.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Not recorded  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Not recorded  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  
  - Advised to contact support line to organize blood tests.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  
  - Follow-up after blood results via text prompt; earlier review if symptoms worsen or new red flags emerge.

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Not recorded  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not recorded  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Major depressive disorder (High): Persistent low mood, low energy, decreased appetite, weight loss, and sexual difficulties over months support depression.  
- Hypothyroidism relapse due to stopping levothyroxine (Medium): Known hypothyroidism with cessation of therapy; symptoms of fatigue and low mood align, though weight loss is atypical.  
- Situational panic/claustrophobia (Medium): Palpitations and dyspnea specifically in elevators with normal exertional tolerance suggest situational anxiety/panic.

Quality checks

- Missing but clinically expected elements:  
  - Vitals (BP, pulse), anthropometrics (weight, BMI, waist), full medication list, allergies, comprehensive mental health screening (PHQ-9/GAD-7, suicidality), immunization review (influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus), fasting glucose/lipids, thyroid function tests, urinalysis, ECG consideration, cancer screening (FOBT), bone health evaluation.  
- Internal conflicts or contradictions:  
  - Hypothyroidism typically causes weight gain; patient reports weight loss (conflict noted).  
  - Clinician noted palpitations align more with hyperthyroidism/anxiety, yet patient is off levothyroxine (conflict noted).  
- Transcript quality notes:  
  - Telehealth; no physical exam performed.  
  - Patient age stated as 35 years, which does not align with “Adults 55 years and older” assessment template.  
  - Some responses were unclear or incomplete; exact timelines and quantities are approximate.
